items.title: No retrieved evidence on programme adaptations
items.whyItMatters: The recorded search returned nothing and the four leads are unchecked, so no adaptation can be called evidence-based.
items.opportunity: Check the leads by identifier before citing them and treat the local study as the main source of evidence.

items.title: Nothing is known about people who leave
items.whyItMatters: Outcomes are collected only at the first and last session, so the benefit of the programme is measured only in those who stay.
items.opportunity: Add a brief outcome check and a short conversation at the point of leaving and at three months.

items.title: Barriers by work, transport and language are assumed
items.whyItMatters: The adaptations target barriers that have never been measured; if the assumptions are wrong the changes will not help the people most affected.
items.opportunity: Record employment, travel mode and language at referral and report completion by each.

items.title: Adaptations may dilute the group
items.whyItMatters: Video participants may lose group connection, which may be part of the benefit.
items.opportunity: Measure group connection and fidelity to the core content in adapted and standard groups.

items.title: Staff hours for evening groups are not approved
items.whyItMatters: The evening group cannot run without the clinic manager's approval.
items.opportunity: Sequence the adaptations so the orientation call and hybrid option can start first.

errorsFound: The need implies the three changes will raise completion; there is no retrieved evidence for any of them.
reevaluation: With nothing retrieved, the gaps favour an implementation study that measures the barriers, follows people who leave and introduces the adaptations in sequence.
summary: Five gaps; the empty search and the missing data on people who leave are high severity.
